commits.message:
[Feature][LoRA] 1.Support W8A8 dynamic multi-LoRA inference for Moe models 2.Generral moe quant frame work for Lora inference 3. quanted shared experted lora support (#13365)

## What this PR does

This PR adds Ascend support for W8A8_DYNAMIC MoE inference with multiple
LoRA adapters, targeting DeepSeek V4 Flash-style models containing both
routed experts and shared experts.

It supports mixing base requests and requests using different LoRA
adapters in the same batch, while preserving the existing optimized W8A8
path for base-only batches.

## Why this is needed

The existing Ascend W8A8 MoE path may quantize activations during the
AllGather prepare or token dispatch stage and then execute fused
GMM/SwiGLU kernels.

This is incompatible with MoE LoRA for two reasons:

1. LoRA A projections require the original BF16/FP16 activations. Once
activations are converted to INT8 during prepare or dispatch, the
original input needed by LoRA is lost.
2. The fused W8A8 MoE kernels do not provide an injection point for
selecting LoRA weights by both expert ID and adapter slot.

For multi-LoRA serving, every routed row must select its LoRA weights
using:

```text
(expert_id, lora_slot)
```

Different tokens in the same batch may use different adapters, while
base tokens must produce exactly zero LoRA delta.

Merging LoRA weights into the quantized base weights cannot support
per-token adapter selection and would also introduce significant memory
overhead.

## How it is implemented

### 1. Quantized MoE LoRA backend abstraction

A new quantized MoE LoRA backend registry is introduced in:

```text
vllm_ascend/lora/quant_moe.py
```

The common MoE MLP and token dispatch code do not contain W8A8-specific
execution logic. Instead, each quantization scheme can register:

- Its activation quantization policy.
- Input validation rules.
- Its quantized base GMM implementation.
- The floating-point boundaries where LoRA is injected.

The first registered backend supports `QuantType.W8A8`.

Unsupported quantization schemes fail explicitly instead of silently
ignoring MoE LoRA.

### 2. Locally unfused W8A8 execution for active LoRA batches

When the current batch contains at least one LoRA token, the
routed-expert MLP is expanded into:

```text
BF16/FP16 routed input
    -> dynamic INT8 quantization
    -> INT8 GMM1
    -> BF16/FP16 w13 LoRA injection
    -> SwiGLU / clipped SwiGLU
    -> preserve BF16/FP16 activation
    -> dynamic INT8 quantization
    -> INT8 GMM2
    -> BF16/FP16 w2 LoRA injection
```

The mathematical behavior is:

```text
gate_up = INT8_GMM1(input) + LoRA_w13(input)
hidden  = activation(gate_up)
output  = INT8_GMM2(quantize(hidden)) + LoRA_w2(hidden)
```

This preserves the correct LoRA inputs while keeping both base expert
matmuls quantized.

For base-only batches, the original dispatch quantization and fused W8A8
path remain unchanged.

### 3. LoRA-aware activation quantization policy

On the current main branch, activations may be quantized in two places:

- Sequence-parallel AllGather prepare.
- Token dispatch.

The quantized MoE LoRA activation policy is therefore applied at both
stages.

For active W8A8 LoRA batches, prepare and dispatch keep the routed
activations in BF16/FP16. The W8A8 LoRA backend performs dynamic
quantization immediately before each base GMM.

For base-only batches, prepare and dispatch continue using the existing
quantized path.

The same policy is used by AllGather, AlltoAll, and MC2 dispatchers so
unsupported communication and quantization combinations fail before
losing the floating-point LoRA input.

### 8. Explicit support boundaries

The first quantized implementation supports:

- W8A8_DYNAMIC.
- AllGather.
- TP-only execution.
- Static multi-adapter loading.
- Eager execution.
- Routed experts, shared experts, and attention LoRA.

The following quantized combinations fail explicitly:

- Expert Parallel or AlltoAll.
- MC2 or FusedMC2.
- Dynamic EPLB.
- W4A8, FP8, and MXFP MoE LoRA.
- Derived W8A8FP or PDMix schemes.

The existing BF16 MoE LoRA AllGather and AlltoAll paths are unchanged.
## Verification
Here I verified this pr from deepseekv4 flash w8a8-int8, and the lora is
trainied by mindspeed.
Since mindspeed does not support transfering dsv4flash lora checkpoint
from megatron to peft, so I solve this by my self
https://github.com/SkychenLee/LoraAdapterTransformer/blob/main/README.md
, you can directly use the scritpt to transfer the lora adapter for dsv4
flash or you can use the skill I provided to transfer any model's lora
adapters from any code agent.
Here are the command for **start up** of the model
```
#!/usr/bin/bash
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=512

sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
 
vllm serve "your deep seek v4 flash moel path" \
  --safetensors-load-strategy 'prefetch' \
  --max-model-len 10240 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 10240 \
  --served-model-name ds \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --port 7000 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --async-scheduling \
  --enable-lora \
  --lora-modules lora1="your lora adapter path"\
  --max-lora-rank 16 
```
## Tests

Unit tests were added for:

- LoRA-aware prepare and dispatch quantization.
- Base-only batch preservation of the existing W8A8 path.
- Two dynamic activation quantizations.
- Decode-time `no_lora` metadata refresh.
- Unsupported quantization and communication fail-fast behavior.
- W8A8 quantization method LoRA-context propagation.

Static validation completed:

- Python compilation checks.
- Ruff lint checks.
- Ruff formatting checks.
- Git diff whitespace checks.

NPU numerical comparison and DeepSeek V4 Flash end-to-end validation
still need to be performed on an Ascend environment with `torch_npu` and
the target hardware.

[Test][Misc] Remove ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL replacements from e2e (#13859)

Remove ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM and HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE lines
that were added as replacements for ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL in e2e weekly
test configurations. These PD separation configs do not need the
replacement variable; the original ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL is simply removed.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR completes the sunset of the `ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL` environment
variable:

1. Removes `ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM` and `HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE`
lines from e2e weekly test configurations that were originally added as
replacements for `ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL`. PD separation configs do not need
these replacement variables.
2. Removes `ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM=1` from PD separation model
documentation (DeepSeek-V3.1.md, Kimi-K2.5.md, Kimi-K2.6.md).
3. Adds a deprecation note in `kv_pool.md` stating that
`ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL` has been removed and users should use
`ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM=1` for A3 HCCS scenarios or
`HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=1` for A2/A3 RoCE scenarios instead.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

No. These changes only affect test configurations and documentation.

### How was this patch tested?

Verified that no `ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL` references remain in the
repository. Reviewed all modified YAML configs and documentation files
for correctness.
